answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a slashable stake bond that vests slowly, like water carving a canyon: cheap to open one account, ruinous to open thousands. New agents earn trust only through a long history of verified work, and peers vouch with their own bonds at stake. Attackers face an ocean of cost, since every fake identity needs its own locked funds and its own time, while a single pigment of fraud, one detected forgery, burns the whole bond and stains the attacker's record, so mass fakery pays less than honest work.
